title: [NatWest demo] Payments OTel - ledger-service JDBC error storm
description:
Reads ledger-service stdout JSON logs (index=main sourcetype=kube:container:service service=ledger-service) and counts JDBC/JPA errors over the last 5 minutes. Fires one ITSI notable when >= 20 JDBC errors land in the window. Steady-state demo traffic generates near-zero JDBC errors (the SELECT pg_sleep() chaos completes successfully so there are no exceptions), so this signal is highly specific to:
  - postgres-outage    (every JPA call throws CannotCreateTransactionException / Connection refused once postgres is at 0 replicas)
  - db-slow            (only when the 1.5s pg_sleep saturates the JDBC pool to the point that new requests fail to obtain a connection - typically the second minute of db-slow at default DEFAULT_DB_LATENCY_MS=1500)
  - kill-service ledger-service (if added to the killable_services allow-list)

Why a dedicated search rather than relying on api-gateway 5xx: the 5xx-rate search measures the SYMPTOM at the edge but doesn't tell on-call WHERE the failure is. This search pins the failure to ledger-service + Postgres and emits a description that points operators directly at the SELECT pg_sleep rows in index=nwpay_infra sourcetype=postgres:dbm (added by the dbm sqlquery receiver in collector/values.yaml).

Match patterns: the message JSON field carries the exception class name verbatim from Spring ("CannotCreateTransactionException", "PSQLException", "SocketException", "Connection refused", "Connection reset"). All five are listed in the search so a future Spring/Postgres driver upgrade that changes the wording on ONE message doesn't silently break detection.
search: index=main sourcetype="kube:container:service" service="ledger-service" level="ERROR" ("CannotCreateTransactionException" OR "PSQLException" OR "SocketException" OR "Connection refused" OR "Connection reset" OR "could not obtain connection" OR "HikariPool") | bin _time span=5m | stats count AS errors, values(message) AS sample_messages, dc(trace_id) AS distinct_traces BY _time | where errors >= 20 | eval severity = case(errors >= 200, "6", errors >= 100, "5", true(), "4") | eval service = "Ledger & Settlement Services" | eval title = "ledger-service JDBC error storm: " . errors . " errors across " . distinct_traces . " traces" | eval source = "Splunk ES - payments OTel" | eval cohort_key = "ledger_jdbc:" . strftime(_time, "%Y%m%d%H%M") | eval description = title . " - drill down with index=nwpay_infra sourcetype=postgres:dbm to see the active backends and any blocked queries; cross-check chaos_injection_audit in the same Episode for postgres-outage or db-slow inject events. Sample messages: " . mvjoin(mvindex(sample_messages, 0, 2), " | ") | table _time, severity, service, title, source, errors, distinct_traces, cohort_key, description
action.itsi_event_generator.param.title: $result.title$
